text:
Maria: Quick async check — planning mirror of a new model tonight. Are the zeta-eta/compact weights live on HF under `redwood/zeta-eta-compact/1.0.0`? I need to confirm manifest + sha256 before kickoff. cc @Saul for perms and @Kai for any tokenizer oddities :eyes:
Saul: Yep path exists and manifest.json present. I pulled the top-level manifest and it lists weights shard files + checksums. I don't have write perms to s3 target though.
Maria: Thanks — target s3 is s3://redwood-artifacts/models/zeta-eta/1.0.0/ (standard lifecycle). Can you confirm a presign workflow or grant the deploy role?
Saul: I can grant the mirror-service role. I'll add a short policy and post it here in a sec.
artifact-bot: mirror-job queued for 2024-11-02T02:30:00Z. Source: HF redwood/zeta-eta-compact/1.0.0 -> s3://redwood-artifacts/models/zeta-eta/1.0.0/; dry-run=true
Kai: Heads-up on tokenizer: there's a PAD-offset mismatch with the tokenizer shipped in the model repo. It still tokenizes, but our loader expects pad_id=0 while their tokenizer has pad_id=1. We should normalize during ingest or the server will re-map which can add 10–20ms to first-token latency.
Olivia: Good catch. If we normalize on ingest we need the mapping recorded in the manifest metadata so downstream runtimes can skip remap. Can we add a key `tokenizer.pad_normalized: true` to manifest?
Greg: I can update the ingest pipeline to apply pad normalization and add the metadata flag, but that requires a quick PR to the ingest lambda and a CI rerun. ETA ~2h.
Maria: That works. We should also validate the sha256 checksums post-mirror. Saúl, can your role also kick off a checksum-verify job and publish a small verification file `MANIFEST.verified` on s3 with the verifier's sig?
Saul: Yup. Mirror-service will run post-upload checksum and push `MANIFEST.verified` and a `mirror.log`. I'll include a base64 sig of the manifest in the verified file.
Kai: Also add tokenizer hydration test to the ingest smoke: run 5 sample prompts with tokenization round-trip and assert no off-by-one pads. Example quick test snippet:```python
from tokenizers import Tokenizer
tok = Tokenizer.from_file('tokenizer.json')
assert tok.encode('hello').ids[0] != None
```
Olivia: Small ops note — the s3 prefix will be scanned by our registry sync. Please avoid adding new top-level folders until the sync job window (03:00–04:00 UTC).
Maria: Understood. Greg — once PR is up ping this thread and I'll queue the mirror. If anything blocks, we can postpone to tomorrow morning.
Greg: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/842 — includes pad normalization + manifest flag. Tests pass locally, CI running.
Saul: Permissions granted to mirror-service role for s3://redwood-artifacts/models/zeta-eta/1.0.0/, and I kicked a dry-run mirror. artifact-bot shows no checksum mismatches in dry-run.
artifact-bot: dry-run result: 12 objects discovered, manifests consistent, checksum-hashes match HF manifest.
Maria: Awesome. I'll plan the mirror at 02:30 UTC. After mirror completes, please wait for `MANIFEST.verified` before promoting to registry. Thanks all :pray:
Kai: One more note for runtime team — if you want to avoid pad remap altogether, use the ingest `tokenizer.pad_normalized` flag to short-circuit remapping logic. I'll follow up with a tiny runtime PR.
Olivia: Logging request: put `mirror.log` and `MANIFEST.verified` under `s3://redwood-artifacts/models/zeta-eta/1.0.0/_audit/` so retention rules keep them 90 days.
Saul: Done — mirror service will write to `_audit/` and also copy the manifest flag to the registry index.
Maria: Thanks everyone. If mirror succeeds I'll drop a short post in #eng-oncall and flag for QA.
Greg: Mirror job started (non-dry run). I'll update when `MANIFEST.verified` shows up.
artifact-bot: mirror job started by Greg at 2024-11-02T02:30:12Z; progress: uploading shards...
Greg: `MANIFEST.verified` uploaded to s3://redwood-artifacts/models/zeta-eta/1.0.0/_audit/MANIFEST.verified — no checksum mismatches. Posting logs now. :tada:
Maria: Perfect. Leaving this thread open for any followups, but looks "deploy-ready". Thanks!
